description: Shared-core plumbing that the in-process pipeline will later consume. Refactor probe.py so Phase B/C run from a shared core; add an in-memory entry point probe_document_images (no fitz, no S3); add magic-byte image-format detection at the VLM boundary; add per-lang caching in scanned._get_paddle_engine; add the settings.probe_enabled flag. This feature touches NO pipeline wiring and leaves the codebase green on its own; FEAT-002 depends on it. The standalone Lambda path (probe_document) must stay byte-for-byte behaviorally identical.
steps: settings flag: in src/config/settings.py add 'probe_enabled: bool = False' into the Core-routing-thresholds block right after 'enable_vlm_direct' (~line 341), matching the existing pydantic-settings style. env_prefix='IDP_' makes it read IDP_PROBE_ENABLED automatically; no _fallback_unprefixed_env entry needed.

probe.py shared-core refactor (NO behavior change to probe_document): extract the inline Phase-B/C logic into internal helpers reused by both entry points. (a) Keep the _observe(pn) logic but make it constructible as a closure/factory over (cfg, vlm, onnx, stats) so both entry points use the SAME lipika-vs-vlm telemetry (logger.info('probe.lipika_vs_vlm', ...)) and the VLM-overrides-confident-latin seam verbatim. (b) Add _sample_and_aggregate(nonblank, jpegs, cfg, vlm, onnx, stats) -> DocPrior wrapping pick_sample_pages -> samples_disagree/additional_sample_pages -> aggregate_doc (the current 'if nonblank and not cache_hit' block, minus the S3 cache write which stays only in probe_document). (c) Add _decide_pages(candidates, nonblank, timed_out, feats, prior, cfg) -> dict[int, PageProbe] wrapping Phase C (_page_values nearest-sample inheritance + decide_route + blank pages + timed_out). probe_document keeps its full signature and still opens fitz, renders, uploads to S3, builds feats/jpegs, does the cache read/write, then calls the shared helpers; its returned dict and stats stay identical.

probe.py new entry point: add def probe_document_images(images, page_numbers, *, profiles=None, cfg, vlm=None, onnx=None, time_left=None) -> dict[int, PageProbe]. images maps page_number -> RGB numpy array OR encoded bytes (PNG/JPEG); decode bytes via cv2.imdecode + cv2.cvtColor(...COLOR_BGR2RGB) (reuse the _gray_mask_from_jpeg decode style) when not already an ndarray. Compute Phase-A signals per image IN MEMORY (imaging.analysis_gray + imaging.ink_mask + cv_features.ink_ratio for blank + cv_features.detect_table) and encode a per-page JPEG via imaging.encode_jpeg ONLY to feed _observe (NO S3 put, NO upload pool; image_s3_* stay None/absent). candidates = the page_numbers passed in (caller already filtered with needs_probe). Then call the SAME _sample_and_aggregate and _decide_pages helpers from the previous step. profiles is optional metadata only. Return {page_number -> PageProbe}. No fitz, no render_rgb-from-PDF, no S3, no cache.

vlm_probe.py magic-byte detection: in BedrockScriptProbe._call, detect the format from the leading bytes -> b'\x89PNG' => 'png', b'\xff\xd8\xff' => 'jpeg', else/ambiguous => 'jpeg' (preserves the Lambda path which feeds real JPEG). Pass the detected string into the Converse {'image': {'format': <fmt>, 'source': {'bytes': ...}}} block. Keep raw bytes (no decode/re-encode). Leave observe(page_number, jpeg) signature unchanged. CHOSEN APPROACH: magic-byte detection (lighter than re-encode).

scanned.py per-lang cache: change _get_paddle_engine signature to _get_paddle_engine(mode: str = 'printed', lang: str = 'en'); key the _paddle_engines cache by (mode, lang) instead of mode; pass lang=lang into BOTH PaddleOCR(...) constructors (printed + handwritten). In _ocr_convert, change the local-fallback call to engine = _get_paddle_engine(mode=mode, lang=(ocr_lang or 'en')). Leave low_confidence_word_ratio's _get_paddle_engine(mode='printed') as-is. Do NOT touch any other ocr_lang plumbing or the Lambda payload (already done).

NEW unit test file tests/test_probe_inprocess_images.py (mock Bedrock via a StubVLM like tests/test_probe.py; onnx None or a fake peaking session like tests/test_probe.py _onnx_peaking; NO Paddle/AWS/torch). Cover: probe_document_images with numpy RGB inputs -> latin->paddleocr_printed+ocr_lang 'en', non-latin(devanagari/telugu)->vlm_transcribe, blank->skip; probe_document_images with PNG-bytes and with JPEG-bytes inputs decode and route identically; BedrockScriptProbe._call magic-byte detection via a fake client recording the format field (assert 'png' for PNG bytes, 'jpeg' for JPEG bytes, 'jpeg' for ambiguous); VLM call count == n_samples (3) for a multi-page latin doc and MORE than 3 when samples disagree (StubVLM per_page map returns latin vs devanagari) with non-sampled pages inheriting nearest sample; _get_paddle_engine caches a distinct engine per (mode, lang) asserted via a monkeypatched fake PaddleOCR constructor that records lang (do NOT import real paddleocr).
acceptance_criteria: Running '.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_probe.py -q' passes with the same count as baseline (the standalone probe_document Lambda path is unchanged).
Running '.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "from src.config.settings import settings; print(settings.probe_enabled)"' prints False.
Running '.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import inspect, src.ai.layer2_conversion.scanned as s; print(inspect.signature(s._get_paddle_engine))"' shows (mode: str = 'printed', lang: str = 'en').

Running '.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_probe_inprocess_images.py -q' passes all new tests, including the magic-byte format assertions and the VLM-call-count (==3, and >3 on disagreement) checks.
No edits outside src/ai/layer1_probe/*, src/ai/layer2_conversion/scanned.py, src/config/settings.py, and the new test file; no .onnx touched; src/api/lambda_probe_handler.py untouched.
verification: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_probe.py tests/test_probe_inprocess_images.py tests/test_probe_linewise.py tests/test_probe_script_onnx.py -q -m "not slow"
findings:
FEAT-002 handoff:

(1) New entry point signature: probe_document_images(images: dict[int, np.ndarray|bytes], page_numbers: list[int], *, profiles: dict[int, Any]|None = None, cfg: ProbeConfig, vlm: Any = None, onnx: Any = None, time_left: Callable[[], float]|None = None) -> dict[int, PageProbe]. Keyed by page_number. images values may be an RGB uint8 ndarray OR encoded PNG/JPEG bytes (decoded via cv2.imdecode + BGR->RGB). candidates = [pn for pn in page_numbers if pn in images]; caller MUST pre-filter with needs_probe (pass profile.model_dump() as the profile dict, given_route from router.route_from_profile). No fitz/S3/cache; image_s3_* stay None. Any per-page render error -> PageProbe(status='error', route='paddleocr_printed'); the whole doc never aborts.

(2) Shared-core hook names in probe.py (reuse from the pipeline wiring; do NOT re-inline): _make_observe(cfg, vlm, onnx, jpegs, stats) -> _observe closure (holds the probe.lipika_vs_vlm telemetry + VLM-overrides-confident-latin seam); _sample_and_aggregate(nonblank, jpegs, cfg, vlm, onnx, stats) -> DocPrior; _decide_pages(candidates, nonblank, timed_out, feats, prior, cfg, given=None, image_keys=None, img_bucket=None) -> dict[int, PageProbe]. Also _rgb_from_image(img) decodes ndarray-or-bytes. probe_document is unchanged behaviorally (still renders via fitz, uploads, reads/writes the S3 cache) and now calls these same helpers; tests/test_probe.py stays green (49 passed, incl. the Lambda handler path).

(3) PageProbe -> page_context['probe'] dict fields FEAT-002 must attach per probed page (exactly): route, ocr_lang, script, script_confidence, handwriting_prob, has_table, is_blank, route_reason. PageProbe exposes all of these (PageProbe.route is ALREADY an engine-name string: skip | paddleocr_printed | paddleocr_handwritten | vlm_transcribe -> use directly as EngineTask.engine; do NOT remap through pipeline._ROUTE_TO_ENGINE). Pages PageProbe.status=='not_needed' (digital/blank passthrough) must get NO 'probe' key. Non-probed statuses to be aware of: 'blank' -> route 'skip'; 'error'/'skipped_timeout' still carry a route.

(4) scanned._get_paddle_engine is now (mode: str='printed', lang: str='en'); engines cached per (mode, lang); _ocr_convert local fallback calls lang=(ocr_lang or 'en'). The ocr_lang Lambda-payload plumbing was already done; untouched.

(5) vlm_probe.BedrockScriptProbe._call now detects PNG (b'\x89PNG')/JPEG (b'\xff\xd8\xff') via BedrockScriptProbe._image_format(data) (ambiguous -> 'jpeg') and passes it as the Converse image format. observe() signature unchanged. CHOSEN APPROACH: magic-byte detection (no re-encode). Pipeline supplies PNG bytes today; this makes them valid to the VLM.

(6) settings.probe_enabled: bool = False added (env IDP_PROBE_ENABLED via env_prefix='IDP_'). FEAT-002 gates the new per-document probe on settings.probe_enabled.

(7) VLM calls per document in tests = n_samples (3) for a homogeneous multi-page latin doc; >3 (up to max_samples=6) only when the first-wave samples disagree. blank pages are never sampled.

(8) BASELINE test count before FEAT-001: tests/test_probe.py = 49 passed (1 deselected slow). FEAT-001 verification suite (test_probe + test_probe_inprocess_images + test_probe_linewise + test_probe_script_onnx, -m 'not slow') = 62 passed after FEAT-001 (13 new in test_probe_inprocess_images.py). The repo-wide full fast suite was not run to green here: it hangs on unrelated heavy/real-engine or network tests outside FEAT-001 scope; the targeted probe/pipeline/scanned suites all pass.

NOTE: settings.py also carries PRE-EXISTING uncommitted S3-storage fields (s3_bucket/s3_region/s3_documents_prefix) authored before this feature; only the probe_enabled flag belongs to FEAT-001.
